title: Recursive Efficiency Program - Wave 4 Convergence Report

lessons_learned: Build/Integrate/Harden/Activate is an effective 4-wave progression. Each wave has a distinct purpose and natural dependencies on prior waves.
Wiring wave (Wave 4) required fewer new lines (~800) than any prior wave but touched the most critical code paths. Integration risk was higher than construction risk.
Quality gate as forcing function: the 44.9% -> 98.4% -> 100% progression gave every team a measurable target.
Pre-commit hooks are the final defense against regression. Without them, the 100% quality gate would decay over time.
Deferred work is acceptable: Team Tango's stress test was correctly deprioritized to ensure the wiring was done first.
3-agent teams (lead + 2 devs) worked consistently across all 20 teams in all 4 waves.
